source.title: Mechanistic Analysis Of Universality: Numerical Comparison Circuits Across Transformer Architectures
source.authors: Arya Bhardia; Julian Ramirez; Siddhanta Verma; Karen Mkrtchyan

record.tranche_reason: The study investigates circuits for numerical comparison, not indirect object identification. Its results do not test whether the IOI circuit or its roles hold.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the IOI study among prior interpretability work, but does not test IOI. Its numerical-comparison findings are recorded under fits_no_version because they concern circuit universality for a related but different task.
record.test_reason: The study finds circuits for 4-digit numerical comparison in Qwen, Llama and Gemma models. It cites the IOI paper only as the source of path patching. No result concerns IOI, its head classes, backup heads, or IOI evaluation sensitivity. V3's reuse clause would need IOI head classes reused for this task, and none is examined.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors find a localized, consistent numerical-comparison circuit within Qwen models, and a distributed, earlier-emerging signal in Llama3-8b-instruct and Gemma2-9b-instruct. They conclude that similar task accuracy does not imply mechanistic universality.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses activation patching, path patching, DLA, PCA, and steering on numerical-comparison prompts rather than investigating the IOI task or its circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different localization patterns across model families; it does not report sensitivity tests of the IOI circuit's evaluation choices.

fits_no_version.finding: For 4-digit numerical comparison, Qwen models (1.7b–7b) show one or two localized late attention heads that write a separable greater-than signal, fed by a mid-layer sender head.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Numerical-comparison circuits are localized and structurally consistent within the Qwen family.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama3-8b-instruct and Gemma2-9b-instruct, top head scores are not sharply distinguished from other heads. Class separation appears earlier in the residual stream, so the computation looks distributed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuit localization for a task does not transfer across model families despite similar accuracy, which bears on circuit universality in general.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, Student Research Workshop
record.problems: The paper states that it could not reliably identify specific components for path patching and neuron-level DLA in Llama3-8b-instruct and Gemma2-9b-instruct. It notes that a more diverse prompt set or additional methods could address limitations. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No further numerical-comparison results were extracted, including the benchmark accuracy table, PCA plots, steering plots, neuron DLA details, and additional path-patching edges; these do not bear on the IOI claim versions.

untested.parts: All: the IOI circuit in GPT-2 small, its 26 heads in 7 classes, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
All: backup name-mover heads after ablation.
All: IOI circuits in other models, sizes or checkpoints, and reuse of IOI components for other tasks.
All: whether other methods, ablations or metrics recover the IOI circuit.
All: sensitivity of IOI circuit evaluation to ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
All: IOI prompt variants such as name orders, templates and more names.

record.verdict_notes: The IOI paper is cited only as the method reference for path patching. The study's cross-family universality result concerns a different task and is not an IOI-circuit result, so it is placed under fits_no_version rather than V3.
